messages:
incident-bot: 🔴 ALERT: Elevated 5xx + p99 latency spike detected in us-east-1 for Hosted API and several Dedicated pools. Signal: increased 5xx rate from auth/egress and observability ingestion errors. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood-inference/internal/d/alerts?panelId=432
alex: acked. paging devon and eng-runtime. I'll grab initial triage.
devon: I see spikes across router and model-proxy -- large fraction 502/503 coming from upstream STS/KMS egress timeouts, also high error rate from our observability forwarder (CWL/ELB).
julia: confirm evicted KV cache logs show `UpstreamError: connect timeout` around 23:02 UTC.
mina: impact: hosted API error rate ~8% for us-east-lb, Dedicated pool eu-west unaffected but us-east dedicated pools seeing elevated tail latency and instability. Customer-facing traffic to hosted in us-east ~35% of global.
samir: tried tailing proxy logs: 
```
[23:01:45] proxy: upstream call failed: Get https://sts.amazonaws.com/: dial tcp 18.203.x.x:443: i/o timeout
[23:02:01] runtime: model shard read latency spike > 200ms
```
beth: support-bot reported 4 high-sev customer tickets (feature generation timeouts). Customers hitting Hosted API are seeing 5xx and timeouts. Need status page update.
alex: immediate mitigation plan: 1) enable regional routing fallback to us-west-2 for Hosted API traffic; 2) shift Dedicated pool routing off affected us-east compute nodes to warm replicas in us-west and eu-west; 3) disable observability forwarding to third-party (buffer locally) to relieve egress.
devon: executing step 1 now: flipping routing policy for non-geo-locked customers to prefer us-west-2. Command: `infractl routing set-policy --region-preference us-west-2 --scope hosted-api --expedited`
eng-runtime: confirmed we have compatible model variants in us-west-2 for the top 10 models. Will start warmup of additional replicas, pre-populating KV caches.
julia: step 2: placing affected Dedicated nodes into maintenance to prevent new sessions, migrating existing sessions where feasible. Running: `dedicatedctl drain --pool us-east-1a --grace 90s`
mina: step 3: disable obs forwarder to 3rdparty temporarily: `obsctl forwarder disable --target cwl --region us-east-1` — logs now buffered to S3 fallback for 1h TTL.
samir: net result so far: 30% of hosted requests now routed to us-west-2; observed 40% reduction in 5xx within 2 mins for traffic shifted. Latency for remaining us-east traffic still elevated.
beth: sending initial status update to customers: "We're investigating elevated errors in us-east-1 impacting API requests. We've activated fallback routing and are mitigating. No data loss expected; more updates in 30m."
support-bot: posted incident on status.redwood.ai/incidents/RE-3381 and created incident ticker RE-3381.
alex: ops note: prepare potential throttle and soft-fail policy for Hosted API to switch from 5xx->429 for best-effort clients. We should avoid broad 503s.
eng-runtime: implementing adaptive throttle: `api-gateway update-policy --on-error 5xx => retry->prefer-429` (will push in 2 minutes).
devon: observed one Dedicated customer (acct: 9876) on reserved capacity in us-east showing errors. Reached out to account CSM to coordinate failover; offering dedicated warm replicas in eu-west as temporary.
julia: oncall swap: devon staying until 00:00 UTC, julia will take 00:00-04:00 UTC handover. devon to summarize next.
devon: SUMMARY: root cause appears correlated with AWS STS/KMS egress errors combined with downstream observability ingestion backpressure causing increased proxy timeouts in us-east. Mitigations in progress: route traffic to other regions, drain/evacuate affected dedicated nodes, buffer observability to S3, enable adaptive throttle, warm model replicas in us-west-2. Early impact reduced for shifted traffic.
mina: action items assigned: devon (triage + handoff notes), eng-runtime (warm replicas + kernel tuning), ops (customer comms + CSM outreach), support (update tickets, canned responses).
samir: small follow-up: found increased SYN_RECV on nat gateways in us-east — could be throttling at egress. Filing support case with cloud provider. Case: AWS-RE-2026-3381.
beth: queued status update to customers in 20m with current mitigation details.
support-bot: alerted legal & trust for any potential compliance implications.
alex: escalation: if 5xx persists >30m for global >3% we trigger incident bridge and exec notify. For now stay in-channel.
eng-runtime: metrics: p50/p95 improving for shifted traffic; global 5xx dropped from 8% -> 5% after first routing change. Still above normal baseline.
mina: decision log: do NOT rotate keys or change KMS config during mitigation window; that might spike auth calls. We need to minimize STS calls — enable token cache TTL increase for api-proxies: `authctl cache-ttl set --service proxy --ttl 30m`.
devon: performing controlled token cache TTL bump now.
julia: taking over monitoring. devon please drop handoff summary in #incidents and ping me when you step out.
devon: handoff: I've documented all commands run, links to dashboards, and current status in the incident tracker RE-3381. Key links: grafana panel, routing job id 7321, dedicated drain job 7234. I'm stepping off now — julia oncall.
julia: ack — I have all links. devon thanks. I'll keep monitoring and will escalate to bridge if we see any regression.
alex: post-incident comms plan: once stable, run a postmortem focusing on: STS egress resilience, observability backpressure patterns, routing fallback automation, and dedicated pool multi-region failover runbook.
beth: noted — support will prepare customer follow-up template and map affected customers for outreach.
eng-runtime: small change: enabling KV cache prefetch for warmed replicas to reduce cold-start impact: `runtimectl prefetch --models top10 --region us-west-2`.
mina: ETA for normalcy: if no new upstream egress issues, expect most traffic stable in 30-45 minutes. Will update status page in 20.
support-bot: status page updated: "Mitigations in place — routing fallback and dedicated draining active. Customers may see intermittent errors while we stabilize."
alex: closing notes: keep this thread for the oncall handoff. If you need bridge, run `incident-bot bridge create RE-3381`.
julia: will keep monitoring. ping me for any regressions. :thumbsup:
